title: Prophylactic intrapericardial placement of a pigtail catheter during cardiac surgery involving median sternotomy and extracorporeal circulation to prevent pericardiocentesis or rethoracotomy due to postthoracotomy syndrome
summary:
To prevent blood and fluid from accumulating in the wound area after heart surgery, large-bore drains are inserted into the pericardium and, if opened, also into the pleura during cardiac surgery and placed under suction. Once the flow rates have decreased, these drains are quickly removed to allow the patient to mobilize. 
In some of the patients who have undergone surgery, however, significant fluid accumulates in the pleura and/or pericardium (postthoracotomy syndrome) during the course of their hospital stay. Unlike pericardial effusions, pleural effusions can be punctured or drained using a small-caliber catheter with relatively little risk. Pericardial effusions, on the other hand, pose a challenge in this scenario. Often, there is no safe puncture window in patients with significant pericardial effusion. There is a risk of damaging not only the heart but also the liver during puncture. For this reason, approximately 80% of affected patients whose pericardial effusion compresses the heart require reoperation. In most cases, pericardial effusions are then relieved via a lateral thoracotomy. In these cases, the length of hospital stay is significantly longer and the recovery time is considerably extended.
The planned study aims to examine whether the preventive insertion of a small-caliber catheter (pigtailcatheter) into the pericardium during surgery can spare affected patients from pericardiocentesis or surgical drainage of the pericardium during their hospital stay.

interventions.name:
During the operation, access to the heart is gained by making a median sternotomy, and the use of a heart-lung machine is planned. The operation will be performed as usual. 
Immediately before the thorax is closed, the study participants will be randomly assigned to one of two treatment groups. One
No additional pigtail catheter is used in the control group.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Heart surgery with a heart-lung machine via a median sternotomy
Exclusion criteria:
-Minors
-Patients incapable of giving consent
-Emergency patients
-Patients who have undergone previous surgery
-Dialysis patients
-Patients with ECLS or Impella
